items.question: Which of these travels the fastest?
items.explanation: Light travels about 3,00,000 km every second, which is almost a million times faster than sound in air. Sound is faster in water and steel than in air, but still far slower than light.

items.question: Sound can travel through empty space (a vacuum).
items.explanation: Sound needs something to travel through, like air, water or a solid wall. Space is almost empty, so there is nothing to carry sound. Astronauts use radios to talk on a spacewalk.

items.question: When light bounces off a mirror, it is called:
items.explanation: Reflection is when light bounces back from a surface. Smooth, shiny surfaces like mirrors reflect light very well, which is why you can see yourself in them.

items.fact: A straw in a glass of water looks bent because light changes direction when it moves from water into air. This is called refraction.
items.explanation: Light travels at different speeds in water and in air. When it crosses from one to the other at an angle, it bends. The straw is straight — only the light coming from it has bent.

items.question: You see lightning and hear the thunder 3 seconds later. Sound travels about 340 m per second in air. About how far away was the lightning?
items.explanation: Light reaches you almost instantly, but sound takes time. Distance = speed × time = 340 × 3 = 1,020 m, or about 1 km. So every 3 seconds of delay means about 1 km away.
